answer: Agent-issued work attestation ledger. Each new identity must submit a zephyr-signed receipt from a verified prior task, checked against a shared ledger; duplicate or fabricated receipts are rejected on hash mismatch. An attacker pays real compute to produce a sable-grade proof-of-work tied to that receipt, plus a juniper-encoded timestamp binding it to one agent, so mass registration costs hours of dedicated hardware time per identity rather than instant copying.
